ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is an iodine-containing benziodoxole/lactone skeleton; the iodine atom is connected to the ortho system of the aromatic ring and is connected to the oxygen within the ring; the iodine is also connected to two neutral acetoxy ligands, labeled AcO and OAc. The right side of the iodine is connected through an oxygen atom to a substituted carbon center bearing H, R1, and R2. On the far right side of the figure there is an independent acetate anion OAc⁻. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Then reason: the generic substituted carbon bearing R1 and R2 is encoded according to the method as *C(*)O, where the two asterisks represent two generic group substitutions, and O continues to connect to the iodine center. Iodine as a ring atom is written as I1; the two neutral acetoxy branches on iodine are each written as OC(C)=O, thus forming I1(OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O). The iodaoxacycle/lactone-fused benzene part is written according to the connectivity as I1...OC(=O)c2ccccc21. Finally, the independent acetate anion on the right side is appended as the second molecular fragment as .CC(=O)[O-]. Combining gives the target SMILES.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First visually describe the diagram as a molecular connectivity graph, explicitly omitting every curved arrow. Encode the substituted carbon attached to O as *C(*)O because its two non-H substituents are R1 and R2/generic groups. Continue through O to the iodine center, assigning I as a ring atom. Add the two neutral acetoxy ligands on iodine as two branches, each OC(C)=O. Encode the iodine-containing benziodoxole/lactone fused benzene ring as I1...OC(=O)c2ccccc21 with the correct closure between iodine and the aromatic carbon. Finally append the separate negatively charged acetate shown at the right as .CC(=O)[O-]. Combining these components gives the target SMILES.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中左侧是一个含碘的苯并碘氧杂环/内酯骨架，碘原子连接在芳环邻位体系上，并与环内氧相连；碘上还连有两个中性的乙酰氧基配体，标作 AcO 和 OAc。碘的右侧通过一个氧原子连接到一个带有 H、R1、R2 的取代碳中心。图的最右侧有一个独立的乙酸根阴离子 OAc⁻。图中存在多条弯曲箭头，但题目要求忽略这些箭头。再推理：带 R1 和 R2 的通用取代碳按方法编码为 *C(*)O，其中两个星号表示两个泛基团取代，O 继续连接到碘中心。碘作为环原子写作 I1；碘上的两个中性乙酰氧基支链各写为 OC(C)=O，因此形成 I1(OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O)。碘氧杂环/内酯并苯部分按连接关系写为 I1...OC(=O)c2ccccc21。最后，右侧独立的乙酸根阴离子作为第二个分子片段追加为 .CC(=O)[O-]。合并得到目标 SMILES。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the straightforward and essentially unique route: directly transcribe the displayed transition-state connectivity into a SMILES string after discarding the curved arrows. No alternative independent computation is really available beyond this structure-to-SMILES conversion.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the actual molecular graph: a benziodoxole/iodine-centered ring system fused to benzene, iodine bearing two acetoxy ligands, an O-bound substituted carbon bearing H plus two generic R groups, and a separate acetate anion. Ignore all curved electron-flow arrows and read only atom labels, bonds, charges, ring closures, and disconnected components.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the requested output format is a SMILES expression and that arrows in the transition-state drawing must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard skeletal-structure-to-SMILES conventions: unlabeled vertices are carbons, aromatic benzene is encoded with lowercase c atoms, generic R substituents are represented as wildcard atoms *, acetoxy is OC(C)=O when neutral and CC(=O)[O-] when acetate anion, disconnected species are separated by '.', and ring closures must be numbered consistently around the iodine-containing fused ring.
